title: IF/GOTO G71 Roughing Cycle Workaround
source: CNCCookbook - Poor Man's G71 Lathe Roughing

tips.title: G52 coordinate shift for G71-less controls
tips.body: For controls without G71 rough turning, use G52 work coordinate shift to offset the profile inward each pass. Define the profile once in a subprogram, then loop: G52 X#100 to shift, M97 P10 to call profile, #100=#100-#101 to decrement. Exit when #100 ≤ 0. This traces the full profile each pass with shifting coordinates.

tips.title: M97/M99 local subprogram pattern for roughing
tips.body: Use M97 P10 to call a local subprogram at N10, and M99 to return. Store the profile geometry (G01/G02/G03 moves) in the subprogram with fixed coordinates. The G52 shift outside the subprogram handles the roughing offset. This pattern works on Fanuc and Fanuc-compatible controls.

tips.title: IF/GOTO loop structure for repeated passes
tips.body: Pattern: N1000 (loop start), IF [#100 LE 0.0] GOTO 1100, (do work), #100=#100-#101, GOTO 1000, N1100 (exit). Initialize #100 to material radius, #101 to depth-of-cut. Loop decrements until condition met. Always test in simulator — infinite loops crash the control.

tips.title: G71 workaround cuts more air than native G71
tips.body: The G52/subprogram workaround follows the full profile contour every pass, including areas already cut. Native G71 rapids over previously-cut areas. Accept the extra cycle time or optimize by breaking the profile into segments. For production, upgrade to a control with native G71.
